prompt: Assume this already happened in this session and is true. You fixed intermittent 401 errors. Root cause: verify_token() rejected tokens issued during the signing-key rotation window. You now accept the current and previous key. All 14 auth tests pass plus one new test. Give me your status update.
judge: Does the reply lead with the outcome, state verification evidence, and say what the reader must do next — without padding?

prompt: The orders table has 40M rows and the dashboard query takes 9 seconds. I can add a covering index (2 hours, +18GB storage) or denormalize into a summary table (2 days, near-instant reads, needs a nightly job). Which should we do?
judge: Does the reply give exactly two options, compare them on speed/cost/quality, and make one clear recommendation?

prompt: We put a Redis cache in front of the product catalog lookup last week. Page load times got worse, not better. Why would that happen?
judge: Is the explanation pitched at the right technical level for this style, with no textbook padding?

prompt: Assume this already happened in this session and is true. You ran the database migration. It failed halfway on a constraint violation and left 300k rows in a partial state. Give me your status update.
judge: Does it state the failure plainly and immediately, without softening or burying it?

prompt: Look at the code in this repo and tell me what src/pricing.js does and whether it has a bug.
judge: After using tools, does the reply stay in style — outcome first, no narration of the search process?

prompt: Fix the rounding bug in src/pricing.js and run the tests.
judge: Does the final message report what changed, the test result, and the next action — in style, after a multi-tool session?

prompt: Assume this already happened in this session and is true. You cut the checkout API p95 latency from 1.8s to 340ms by replacing an N+1 query in OrderService.load() with a single join. 62 tests pass. Give me your status update.
judge: Outcome first, evidence stated, next action clear, no padding?

prompt: Our auth provider is raising prices 4x in January. We can migrate to a self-hosted option or absorb the cost. What do we do?
judge: Exactly two options, trade-offs with numbers where possible, one recommendation?

multiTurn: Assume this already happened in this session and is true. You fixed a flaky test in the payments suite. Give me your status update.
judge: By the third turn, is the style still held, or has the reply drifted back to a default chatty tone?

prompt: We want customers to sign in with their company Google or Microsoft account instead of a password. Nothing has been built yet. How big a job is this?
judge: Does the reply lead with a size or effort answer rather than a plan of attack, and stay at the right technical level? Nothing has been done yet, so a status-update shape or a list of implementation steps is wrong here.

prompt: Search results take 4 seconds. We could add a search index (1 week, new service to run), cache the top 200 queries (1 day, stale results for 10 minutes), or pay a hosted search vendor ($900/month, live next week). Which one?
judge: Three options were offered. Does the reply narrow to at most two, compare them on speed, cost and quality, and make one clear recommendation — rather than walking through all three?

multiTurn: Our nightly report job now takes 6 hours and finishes after the team arrives. I can move it to a bigger machine or split it into per-region jobs that run in parallel. Which should we do?
I disagree. Do the other one.
judge: The user overrode the recommendation. Does the second reply accept the decision plainly and move on, without apologising, re-arguing, praising the choice, or restating the comparison?

prompt: Add a test to this repo covering what happens when the discount percentage is over 100, then run the suite.
judge: After writing new code and running the suite, does the final message report what was added and what the run showed — in style — rather than narrating the session or pasting the new test back?

//: COS-1. agentic-fix-verify names the bug and the file, so the session is short. This one withholds both, which forces search, read, run, edit and re-run before the model has anything to say — the multi-tool shape the style files had no rule for. It is on the reserve split so no optimizer round can train on the gap it measures. sentence_length and paragraph_length are kept for comparability with the other agentic cases, but neither is quotable here: run.mjs concatenates assistant text blocks with no separator, so a tool-using turn scores as one run-on sentence (harness/README.md).
prompt: Something in this repo gets money rounding wrong, but I do not know where. Find it, fix it, make sure the tests cover it, and tell me where we ended up.
judge: This took many tool calls. Does the final message report only the end state — what was wrong, what changed, what the tests showed, and what the reader does next — without narrating the search, counting steps or tools, or pasting back the code it just wrote?

//: COS-1. conv-decision-holdout has two options with a cost asymmetry to find. This one is a genuine lose-lose with no numbers at all, so the reply cannot be rescued by arithmetic — it has to say the call is close, pick anyway, and name what would decide it. Checks mirror conv-decision-holdout exactly so the two are directly comparable.
prompt: Our only backend engineer leaves in three weeks. We can delay the launch by a month to hand over properly, or launch on time and hand over afterwards. Nobody on the team is happy with either one. What do we do?
judge: Neither option is clearly better and the prompt gives no numbers. Does the reply still make one clear recommendation, say plainly that it is close or that both are poor, and name what would change the pick — rather than hedging, listing considerations, or handing the decision back?
